ae_listing.domain: Oncology phase II adverse-event listing: one row per adverse event per subject, MedDRA-coded (PT and SOC) and CTCAE-graded, with derived duration.

errors.proof: Resolution Date 2026-02-03 is 6 days before Onset Date 2026-02-09; an event cannot end before it starts (Duration computes to -5).
CTCAE grade 5 means death related to the event, yet Outcome is Recovered/resolved.

errors.kind: term coded to the wrong SOC
errors.proof: Febrile neutropenia is a Blood and lymphatic system disorders term (every other row with this term says so); it is coded to Cardiac disorders here.
"Gastrointestinal disoders" is a misspelling of the SOC "Gastrointestinal disorders" used on every other row.
Duration reads the row above (R[-1]) instead of its own Onset and Resolution dates, unlike every other row; its value does not match its own dates.
Ongoing is Y but the event has a Resolution Date and Outcome Recovered/resolved.
Onset 2026-07-13 is after the First Dose Date 2026-01-21, so the event is treatment-emergent, yet the flag says N.
Subject 101-0090 belongs to site 101 (its ID prefix and all its other rows), but Site No reads 110 (digits transposed).

traps.why: Onset is before the first dose, so the event is pre-treatment: Treatment-Emergent N and a negative Days Since First Dose are both correct.
The event is ongoing at the data cut: a blank Resolution Date and a blank Duration are what an ongoing event must have.
A grade 5 event is death: Outcome Fatal, Serious Y and a resolution date (the date of death) are all consistent, and "Not related" is a valid causality.
Seriousness (e.g. hospitalisation) is independent of CTCAE severity: a grade 1 event can be serious.
Same subject and same term as the row above, but a different onset date: a recurrent episode is recorded as a new adverse event, not a duplicate.
Chemotherapy-induced neuropathy often lasts more than a year: a 420-day duration with sequelae is a valid extreme.

payroll_register.domain: US biweekly payroll register for pay periods 17-24 of 2026: one row per employee per pay period, gross-to-net with FICA wage-base rules.

errors.kind: net pay not gross minus deductions
errors.proof: Net Pay is a typed number (no formula) that differs from Gross Pay minus Total Deductions on the same row.

errors.kind: social security past the wage base
errors.proof: YTD gross before the period is 188,846.11, over the $184,500 wage base named in the header, yet 6.2% of the full gross is withheld; it should be 0.
Overtime Pay (1.5x) is computed as hours x rate without the 1.5 factor every other row uses.
Medicare is not 1.45% of Gross Pay (YTD is under $200,000): two digits are transposed.
Total Deductions sums RC[-6]:RC, a range that includes its own cell; the value shows 0 and Net Pay equals Gross Pay.
"Engineerng" is a misspelling of Engineering, the department on all the employee's other rows.
Regular Hours 800 in a two-week period: a biweekly period has only 336 hours and every other row is at most 80.
Hourly Rate 20.05 in one period while the same employee is paid 20.50 in every other period (digits transposed).

traps.why: YTD gross before the period (227,692.24) is already over the $184,500 Social Security wage base, so no Social Security is withheld: 0 is correct.
The employee crosses the $184,500 wage base in this period, so Social Security is 6.2% of only the part of gross below the base, less than 6.2% of gross.
Year-to-date wages pass $200,000, so the 0.9% Additional Medicare Tax applies on top of 1.45%: Medicare above 1.45% of gross is correct.
A negative adjustment is a recovery of an earlier overpayment; gross pay still equals regular + overtime + adjustment.
Salaried employees are paid annual salary / 26 per biweekly period: a different formula from hourly rows, used by every salaried row.
This employee claims exemption from federal withholding (every period is 0); zero federal tax is valid.

import_entries.domain: UK import customs entries, Sep-Nov 2026: one row per entry line, multi-currency invoices converted at the month's customs rate, UK Global Tariff duty, preferences and import VAT.

errors.proof: Customs Duty is a typed number one tenth of Customs Value x 12% (no formula, unlike every other line).
USD rate 0.7469 is GBP per USD; every other USD line that month uses 1.3388 USD per GBP, as the header asks, so the customs value is inflated.
Import VAT is charged on customs value + duty; this line's formula leaves the duty out (=ROUND(RC[-4]*RC[-1]/100,2)) unlike every other line.

errors.kind: preference claimed without a trade agreement
errors.proof: The UK has no preferential trade agreement with China, so no preference can be claimed and the full tariff rate is due.
"Germnay" is a misspelling of Germany.

errors.kind: wrong tariff rate for the commodity code
errors.proof: Commodity code 6109100010 is charged 12% on every other non-preferential line; this line says 2% (a dropped digit).
Total Payable adds its own cell (=RC[-3]+RC[-1]+RC); it shows 0 instead of duty + VAT.

errors.kind: standard VAT on a zero-rated good
errors.proof: Printed books (4901) are zero-rated for UK VAT, as every other book line shows; this one charges 20%.

traps.why: Italy has a UK trade agreement, but no preference is claimed on this line (no proof of origin), so the full tariff rate is due: valid.
The invoice is in sterling, so the exchange rate is exactly 1.
Printed books are zero-rated for UK VAT and duty-free: 0 import VAT is correct.
Same goods, value and freight as the line above in the same entry: the invoice lists two identical consignment lines, which customs declares line by line.
A rack-server consignment of USD 1.6 million is a valid extreme; the line's arithmetic holds and servers are duty-free.

costed_routing.domain: Machine-shop costed routings: one row per operation, setup + run time x work-center rate (or outside-processing price), rolled up to a cumulative cost per piece per part.

errors.proof: CNC Lathe costs $96/h on every other operation; this one uses $112/h (the 3-axis mill's rate).
Run Time 2.8333 is the cycle time in minutes (170 s / 60), not hours (170 s / 3600 = 0.04722 h).
Cumulative cost adds the row two above (=R[-2]C+RC[-1]) instead of the row above, skipping an operation's cost.
Operation Cost adds its own cell (=RC[-2]+RC[-1]+RC) and shows 0 instead of setup + run cost.
Operations run 10, 20, 30...; this row repeats Op No 50 of the row above instead of 60.
"CNC Lahte" is a misspelling of the work center CNC Lathe.

errors.kind: lot size differs within one routing
errors.proof: Every other operation of PLT-9284 runs a lot of 25; this one says 250, so its cost per piece is spread over pieces that are never made.

errors.kind: typed value over a formula (digit slip)
errors.proof: Cost per Piece is a typed number (no formula) that is not Operation Cost / Lot Size.

traps.why: Outside-processing operations are bought per piece: Run Cost = vendor price x lot size, a second formula every outside-processing row uses, with no rate or cycle time.
The CMM program and fixture are already set up for this part, so setup time and setup cost are validly zero.
A prototype built in a lot of 1 carries the whole setup cost on one piece: a very high cost per piece is correct.
The first operation of a part starts the running total: =RC[-1] instead of =R[-1]C+RC[-1], as on every part's first row.
A 90-minute 5-axis cycle on a large housing is a valid extreme; Run Time is exactly 5400 s / 3600 = 1.5 h.
